content:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to apply for the Backend Engineer (Python) role on Tessel Cargo Software’s Routing & Tracking team. With seven years of experience building and operating Java backend services, I would bring experience in event-driven integration, API performance and production reliability to your shipment tracking platform. Tessel’s emphasis on dependable services and teams that own what they run aligns with the production-quality work I value.

At Tejo Insurance Tech, I develop and maintain seven Java 17 and Spring Boot microservices for policy quoting and claims intake. I designed a versioned REST API used by 12 broker partners and introduced idempotent Kafka consumers and an outbox table that eliminated duplicate claim records. I also reduced a quote endpoint’s p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds through Redis caching and JPA query improvements. This experience is directly relevant to building reliable event ingestion and improving the performance of Tessel’s tracking API.

I deploy services to AWS EKS using Helm and Jenkins and participate in a production on-call rota. Previously, at Viajar Online, I built booking and payment features backed by Oracle and used Testcontainers to increase payment module test coverage from 35% to 70%. Alongside my experience with relational databases, Docker and automated delivery, these projects have given me a practical foundation for contributing to Tessel’s production systems.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my backend engineering experience could support the Routing & Tracking team. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well tailored to the Routing & Tracking role. It uses credible, quantified evidence: seven microservices, 12 broker partners, the p99 latency reduction from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds, and test coverage growth from 35% to 70%. It also connects the candidate's Kafka, API, AWS, Kubernetes, testing, and on-call experience to Tessel's production-focused culture without making unsupported claims. The main content limitation is that it does not explicitly name PostgreSQL, despite the candidate having that experience, and it does not clearly frame Java as the comparable backend language accepted by the advertisement. The letter also does not provide evidence of schema migrations, logistics, Python, or the other stated nice-to-have technologies; these are candidate-profile gaps rather than writing defects.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The plain-text structure, standard headings-free letter format, conventional paragraphs, and absence of tables, graphics, columns, or unusual symbols are ATS-friendly. Relevant terms such as Backend Engineer, REST API, OpenAPI, Kafka, Redis, AWS EKS, Helm, Jenkins, Docker, Testcontainers, automated testing, and on-call are present. ATS matching could be improved modestly by adding the supported terms PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, CI/CD, and comparable language/Java in direct relation to the Python requirement. The letter is likely to screen well for a comparable-language interpretation of the role, but Python-specific automated screening may rank it lower because it contains no Python experience or explicit Python-related statement.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows strong alignment with the comparable-language path in the advertisement: seven years of Java backend experience, REST API design, relational databases, query tuning, Kafka, Docker, AWS cloud deployment, Kubernetes/EKS, automated testing, Jenkins-based delivery, and production on-call work. The quantified performance and reliability examples fit the shipment-tracking platform's emphasis on dependable, high-volume services. The culture fit is also credible through references to production quality, service ownership, and on-call responsibility. The candidate's material does not show Python experience or an explicit willingness to work mainly in Python, safe schema migrations, Terraform, observability tooling, logistics or EDI knowledge, or Dutch/French. PostgreSQL is present in the candidate's material but underused in the letter. These are gaps or omissions to interpret separately from the quality of the writing.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR IMPROVEMENT — In the opening paragraph, after "seven years of experience building and operating Java backend services," add a factual phrase such as "Java is the comparable backend language in which I have built production services, including REST APIs, event-driven integrations, and cloud deployments." This makes the qualification pathway explicit without claiming Python experience or unverified willingness.

MINOR IMPROVEMENT — In the third paragraph, change "Alongside my experience with relational databases, Docker and automated delivery" to "Alongside my experience with PostgreSQL and Oracle relational databases, Docker, AWS cloud deployment, Kubernetes, and Jenkins-based CI/CD". Every added technology is supported by the associated CV and improves alignment with the advertisement's terminology.

MINOR IMPROVEMENT — In the second paragraph, change "through Redis caching and JPA query improvements" to "through Redis caching and JPA query tuning". This uses the job advertisement's exact term while remaining faithful to the candidate's documented work fixing N+1 queries and improving JPA queries.

content:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to apply for the Backend Engineer (Python) role on Tessel Cargo Software’s Routing & Tracking team. With seven years of experience building and operating Java backend services, with Java as a comparable backend language used for REST APIs, event-driven integrations and cloud deployments, I would bring experience in event-driven integration, API performance and production reliability to your shipment tracking platform. Tessel’s emphasis on dependable services and teams that own what they run aligns with the production-quality work I value.

At Tejo Insurance Tech, I develop and maintain seven Java 17 and Spring Boot microservices for policy quoting and claims intake. I designed a versioned REST API used by 12 broker partners and introduced idempotent Kafka consumers and an outbox table that eliminated duplicate claim records. I also reduced a quote endpoint’s p99 latency from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds through Redis caching and JPA query tuning. This experience is directly relevant to building reliable event ingestion and improving the performance of Tessel’s tracking API.

I deploy services to AWS EKS using Helm and Jenkins and participate in a production on-call rota. Previously, at Viajar Online, I built booking and payment features backed by Oracle and used Testcontainers to increase payment module test coverage from 35% to 70%. Alongside my experience with PostgreSQL and Oracle relational databases, Docker, AWS cloud deployment, Kubernetes, and Jenkins-based CI/CD, these projects have given me a practical foundation for contributing to Tessel’s production systems.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my backend engineering experience could support the Routing & Tracking team. Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is concise, professional, and well structured. It opens with the target role, presents relevant quantified achievements, and closes appropriately. The strongest evidence includes the REST API used by 12 broker partners, duplicate-record elimination, latency reduction from 1.8 seconds to 450 milliseconds, production on-call experience, and improved test coverage. The letter is also appropriately honest about the candidate's Java background rather than claiming Python experience. A minor limitation is that it relies heavily on technical evidence and could connect the candidate's motivation more explicitly to Tessel's stated engineering values and shipment-tracking context without overstating domain experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is highly parseable: it uses standard paragraphs, no tables or graphics, and includes relevant terms such as backend services, REST API, Kafka, relational databases, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS, Kubernetes, automated testing, CI/CD, Jenkins, and on-call. The wording 'Java as a comparable backend language' is useful for screening against the ad's comparable-language provision. AI/ATS screening probability is strong for a comparable-language backend profile, but weaker for a Python-specific search because the letter contains no Python or FastAPI experience; this is a candidate-profile limitation rather than a document defect. The letter also does not explicitly use the exact phrase 'schema migrations,' but the provided candidate information does not establish that experience, so it should not be added.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns well with the role's backend, REST, event-streaming, PostgreSQL, AWS, Docker/Kubernetes, testing, CI/CD, reliability, and on-call requirements. It also supports Tessel's emphasis on dependable production systems and ownership of operated services. The candidate has seven years of Java backend experience, satisfying the comparable-language experience route, and has fluent English. The main alignment limitations are that the candidate information does not show Python experience or an explicit willingness to work mainly in Python, does not document schema migrations, Terraform, observability tooling, logistics or EDI experience, or Dutch/French. These are profile gaps or unverified requirements, not defects that can be solved by rewriting the cover letter. The letter appropriately avoids claiming them.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR ENHANCEMENT 1 — In the opening paragraph, make the comparable-language qualification slightly more direct and concise. Replace "With seven years of experience building and operating Java backend services, with Java as a comparable backend language used for REST APIs, event-driven integrations and cloud deployments, I would bring experience..." with wording such as: "With seven years of experience building and operating Java backend services—a comparable backend language under your requirements—I would bring proven experience in REST APIs, event-driven integrations, cloud deployment, performance improvement, and production reliability." This removes the repeated "with" construction and makes the ad's comparable-language criterion easier for a recruiter or screening system to identify.

MINOR ENHANCEMENT 2 — In the first paragraph, connect the candidate's demonstrated reliability experience more explicitly to one of Tessel's stated values without claiming unsupported logistics experience. For example, revise the final sentence to: "Tessel's emphasis on dependable services and engineers who own what they run—particularly the value 'Be dependable'—aligns with the production-quality work and on-call responsibility I value." Only use this if the quoted company value is desired; do not add claims about blameless post-mortems, design notes, or logistics systems because they are not supported by the candidate information.
